§6Uranium-233 & Radium-226

§aBred fissile material and the neutron source that starts every reactor.

§6Uranium-233§f (atomic 92):
Unnatural isotope bred from thorium. Fissile component of thorium fuel. Can be bred further into U-235.
Uses: §bThorium fuel§f (primary), §bHEU-233 RBMK fuel§f (linear flux, dangerous), PWR and ZIRNOX fuel, breeding U-235 via breeding reactor.

§6Radium-226§f (atomic 88):
Mildly radioactive (§e7.5 RAD/s§f) uranium/plutonium decay product. From ore processing or cyclotron (carbon box + lead powder).
Uses: §bRa226Be neutron sources§f for RBMK, Research Reactor, and Chicago Pile. Passive flux (constant §e30 output§f), low heat (§e0.035 °C/flux§f), but melting point only §e700°C§f. Also §bRTG pellets§f at §e3 power/tick§f, lasting §e11.5 billion ticks§f (~18 real years). And radium coffee, if you're feeling brave.

§ePS:§f Start breeding Th-232 immediately. The thorium cycle produces more U-233 than it consumes, making it a renewable fuel source for RBMK stabilization.
